one_month_reasoning: The 1-month close is Friday 2026-10-30, because Nov 1 is a Sunday. I now expect no scheduled earnings in the window. Materion has reported Q3 33 days after fiscal quarter end every year 2022-2025 (Oct 29, 2025 after the Sep 26 quarter end) and did the same for Q2 2026 (Jul 3 to Aug 5, date announced Jul 22). Fiscal Q3 2026 ended Oct 2, which points to Wed 2026-11-04, the date MarketBeat also estimates. No date has been announced yet (a search found none), and an announcement would come ~mid-October. The only in-window events are the date announcement itself, the Nov 2 swap expiry (just after the close, immaterial) and macro/semis prints. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways. The stock is at an all-time high after an unexplained +16% two-day move (Oct 1-2; no 8-K, and the Jefferies initiation was already public ~Sep 2), which argues for mild reversal. 12-month momentum is strong, which argues for drift up. Pre-earnings run-up into a Nov 4 print with a beatable bar (H2-implied $3.83, Q3 consensus $1.89) is a mild positive. Net: median ~$308, slightly below spot, with no earnings jump. I use a two-sigma lognormal mixture (70% at 13.5%, 30% at 20%), an effective ~15.5% over 20 trading days, below the 17% from 59%/3.5 because realized vol includes the +30.8% Aug 5 earnings day.

reasoning: Round 2 changes. (1) Facts from the supervisor, checked in my lane. Q3 results are most likely Nov 4, outside the 1-month window: EDGAR 8-K dates follow a strict 33-day rule (Q2 2026: Jul 3 to Aug 5, date released Jul 22), and no Q3 date announcement exists yet. The Jefferies initiation predates the Oct 1-2 jump. The H2 implied guide is $3.83 after H1's $3.17. Guidance was raised once (Q1 8-K reaffirmed $6.00-6.50). Net debt is $420.7M company-defined. Semis are 53.6% of net sales. (2) EPS path moved to consensus: 2027E $8.40 (was $8.30), 2028E $9.66. (3) Comps: 11 listed peers across specialty alloys (CRS, ATI, HWM, KALU), semis materials (ENTG, ESI, MKSI, JX Advanced Metals) and engineered/precious-metal materials (ROG, AME, Umicore). Medians are 28.5x forward P/E and ~18.7x forward EV/EBITDA, with median next-year EPS growth +21% vs MTRN's +20%. MTRN has no structurally higher growth, margin (~10% EBITDA on net sales), returns or lower cyclicality to justify a persistent premium. So both multiples move to the median (P/E 29x -> 28.5x, EV/EBITDA 18x -> 18.7x). (4) DCF weight cut from 20% to 10%, because FCF is only now inflecting. Value $179 -> $173 on the Oct 2027 valuation date. Blended FV rises from $260 to $273. Distribution: three-component lognormal mixture. Bear: 25%, median $190, sigma 0.38. Base: 50%, $290, 0.30. Bull: 25%, $420, 0.28. Overall median ~$293 and P(>= $312) 44% (was 47%). Spot is above FV and above the sell-side average target ($304), so median drift is negative. The fat right tail reflects real momentum in estimates and backlog. The 1-month ladder drops the earnings jump: sigma ~15.5%, median ~$308. Research was limited to ~6 web searches/fetches beyond the peer data pages, and Twelve Data statistics were plan-restricted. Peer forward EV/EBITDA is my derivation from stockanalysis figures (no forward EBITDA consensus available) and JX/Umicore figures are low confidence.

comps_summary.peer_median_growth_next_yr: EPS +21.1% (9 peers with FY2027 EPS consensus); MTRN FY2027 consensus EPS +20.1% ($8.43 vs $7.02), revenue +9.2%
comps_summary.mtrn_today: MTRN at $312.16: 39.4x forward P/E (stockanalysis), ~37x FY2027 consensus EPS; EV $6.99B, about 23.4x my NTM adj EBITDA (~$300M). That is a ~30-37% premium to the peer median P/E and ~25% to median EV/EBITDA.
comps_summary.mtrn_in_my_fair_value: P/E leg: 28.5x NTM (2028E) EPS, equal to the peer median (was 29x). EV/EBITDA leg: 18.7x NTM (2028E) adj EBITDA, equal to the peer median (was 18x). Both are inside the peer range.
comps_summary.justification: I give MTRN no persistent premium or discount to the peer median at the horizon. Growth is in line, not structurally higher: FY2027 consensus EPS growth of +20% is just under the peer median of +21%, and revenue growth of +9% is below most peers. Margins are not structurally better: 23.3% adj EBITDA on value-added sales (Q2 2026) is about 10% of net sales because of pass-through metal, versus ~26% (CRS) and ~19% (ATI) of revenue. The record is cyclical: adjusted EPS was roughly flat over 2022-2025 and FCF only turned up in 2026 (FY2025 ~$24M, H1 2026 $39M), so returns on capital have been modest. The balance sheet is fine (net debt $420.7M, ~1.6-1.9x EBITDA) but no better than peers'. The genuine positives are the beryllium scarcity moat (only Western integrated producer, a customer-funded $65M expansion), RPO up to $116M and backlog +30%. They support today's growth, but I cannot show they make it persistently faster than peers like CRS and ATI, which have their own qualification moats in A&D. The negatives (54% semis exposure, a precision-clad customer problem, small cap) argue more for a discount than a premium. Two things roughly cancel, so I sit at the median. First, the median uses today's peer multiples, and peers trade at cycle-high multiples too, which argues for de-rating by Oct 2027. Second, MTRN's next-year growth is close to the peer median. The current ~37x premium is treated as momentum that should fade, not as fair value.
